clue.text: Make apologies for old lines in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the words are to be heard spoken, not read as spelt

parts.note: old is EX (former) and lines are CUES, an actor's prompts, giving ex-cues

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for an outdated line they said in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: EX (old) plus CUES (lines, as an actor's prompts) said aloud sounds like the word meaning to make apologies for.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse a fault is to offer reasons or apologies on its behalf.

clue.text: Three different points to avoid

parts.note: E and S are compass points, and a cape is a point of land
E and S are compass points, and a cape is a point of land
E and S are compass points, and a cape is a point of land

explanation.surface: Three separate places someone should keep away from.
explanation.walkthrough: The points are of two kinds: compass points E and S, and a headland, CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape something is to avoid or evade it.

clue.text: Recollect what tricky fellow can do on horseback

parts.note: a conjuror is a trickster whose skill is to conjure
a rider in the saddle is said to be up

explanation.surface: Wondering what a trickster could manage while riding a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To conjure up a memory is to call it to mind.

clue.text: Train set

definitions.meaning: a train of attendants is a retinue
a set of rooms or matching furniture

explanation.definitionFit: A suite is both a body of followers and a matched set of things.

clue.text: Cut twice as quickly

indicators.note: twice tells us the word for cut is written out two times in a row

parts.note: to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone told to cut something twice, and fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal command meaning hurry up, i.e. do it fast.

clue.text: Reportedly why female traps a wild animal

indicators.note: traps means the bird word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: reportedly says the word why is taken as heard, giving the letter of the same sound

parts.note: why said aloud is the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a female has caught a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter Y (sounding like 'why') goes inside HEN, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyena is a scavenging carnivore of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Keep trying for each part with energy

parts.note: per means for each
to part is to sever
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Advice to keep going on each section with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to persist despite difficulty.

clue.text: What comes after taking heroin a short time?

definitions.text: What comes after taking heroin a short time?

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
a bit is a short while

explanation.surface: A warning about what follows even brief heroin use.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction that forms after drug use is called a habit.

clue.text: It's quibbling to criticise attempt to muzzle journalist

indicators.note: to muzzle means the word for criticise closes around the journalist

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it
ED is short for editor, a journalist
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to silence a reporter by attacking them is mere hair-splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive fussing over small details.

clue.text: Previous job instrumental in making man retire?

parts.note: last means previous, as in last week
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A former job that helped someone into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is the bugle call sounded at the end of a soldier's day and at funerals, so it is 'instrumental' in sending men to retire.
explanation.definitionFit: This bugle call signals soldiers to retire for the night.

clue.text: An addict treated badly by drug runner

indicators.note: treated badly suggests the letters of an addict are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug runner mistreats a person with an addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated badly' turns AN ADDICT into CANDIDAT; E for ecstasy finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone who runs, or stands, for election.

clue.text: Frenzied attack capturing bishop

indicators.note: capturing means the word for attack holds the bishop letter inside it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A wild assault in which a bishop is seized.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid literally describes a dog with rabies and so means furious or fanatical.

clue.text: Advised puritan to go to part of Bible

parts.note: a prude is a person of puritanical attitudes
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A puritan has been advised to read a section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudent and well-advised both describe sensible, careful action.

clue.text: A couple of ways to introduce a new or ancient language

indicators.note: to introduce says the two road words come before the following pieces

parts.note: two kinds of road: AVE for avenue and ST for street
two kinds of road: AVE for avenue and ST for street

explanation.surface: Two routes are suggested for bringing in a fresh or old tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' means the two roads come first; 'A couple of' reads as part of the definition-like opening but only counts the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the old Iranian language of the Zoroastrian scriptures.

clue.text: Communication during suit telling chap not to pay court

definitions.text: Communication during suit telling chap not to pay court

parts.words: Communication during suit telling chap not to pay court
parts.note: a letter sent while a man is wooing, telling him to stop courting; suit and court sound legal but are about romance

explanation.surface: A legal note during a lawsuit telling a man not to pay court fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' and 'court' look like the law courts, but they mean wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar name for a letter from a woman ending a relationship with her partner.

clue.text: Terrible state of game supported by single people

indicators.note: in a down answer supported by means the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: RU is rugby union
single is one, the Roman numeral I
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A sport in a dire state, propped up by unmarried folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single people' looks like unmarried people, but it is I plus NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is a condition of being ruined, a dire state.

clue.text: What making post mine crookedly could be?

definitions.text: What making post mine crookedly could be?

indicators.note: crookedly means the letters are bent out of order, and also hints at dishonesty

explanation.surface: Wangling a job for oneself dishonestly might be favouritism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crookedly' rearranges POST MINE; dishonestly getting a post would be favouritism.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouring relatives when handing out jobs.

clue.text: Wanted KO, perhaps, before final round in Asian fighting

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the last piece
perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged differently

parts.note: a round shape is O, and final says it comes at the end

explanation.surface: A fighter wanted a knockout before the last round of an Asian bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges WANTED KO into TAEKWOND, then O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tae kwon do is a Korean martial art.

clue.text: Breaking out of this world

explanation.definitionFit: Smashing means both shattering and, colloquially, terrific.

clue.text: Devil or imp — the hopeless sort

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A devil, or a little imp of the hopeless type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' rearranges IMP THE HOPELESS; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the devil to whom Faust sold his soul in legend.

clue.text: Popular school for cricket, say

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a school of thought is a sect

explanation.surface: A fashionable school for cricket, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is the chirping creature, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is one example of a six-legged creature.

clue.text: Take flight

parts.note: read not as flee but as seize a flight, i.e. hijack an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: To skyjack is to seize control of an aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Long anecdote that's without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the anecdote word goes around the point

parts.note: a yarn is a tale
E is a compass point

explanation.surface: A rambling story that has no point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it.

clue.text: Material that's a must for aspiring driver, say?

indicators.note: say means the words are to be spoken, giving the sound of the answer

parts.note: anyone hoping to drive needs a car key

explanation.surface: Asking which fabric a would-be driver must have.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation the fabric sounds like 'car key'.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull brownish cloth used for uniforms.

clue.text: Confused about one's return from dead?

indicators.note: about means the word for confused goes around the letter for one

parts.note: thrown means disconcerted or confused
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a person coming back from the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a ball over the touchline is dead (out of play); a throw-in returns it to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A throw-in is how the ball is put back into play after it leaves the field.

clue.text: Flew, say, over target area

parts.note: ran means hurried, flew

indicators.note: over means the abbreviation for say is turned back to front

parts.note: EG, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Someone flew over a target zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A firing range is an area with targets for shooting practice.

clue.text: Queen in one royal capital of Asian country

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: in means the queen letter is put inside the word for capital

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or capital, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A queen within one of the royal capitals of an Asian land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' here is the adjective meaning excellent, A1, with the 1 written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the nation whose capital is Baghdad.

clue.text: Fool formerly penning article and correspondence

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the word for formerly holds the article

parts.note: once means formerly
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A foolish person once wrote an article and some letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' means a matching of sounds, not letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the matching of vowel sounds in nearby words, a correspondence in sound.

clue.text: Drink served dining at mess

indicators.note: mess means the letters are jumbled, though it reads as a military dining hall

explanation.surface: A drink is served to people eating in the officers' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: GIN AND IT is gin mixed with Italian vermouth. 'mess' is the anagram signal, not the dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cocktail of gin and Italian sweet vermouth.

clue.text: Disgust showed by rejected sweetheart? Exactly!

indicators.note: rejected means the word for sweetheart is turned back to front

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart
to a T means exactly

explanation.surface: A jilted lover shows exactly how disgusted they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns LOVER into REVOL; T comes from 'to a T', exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to sicken or repel them.
